Phishing attacks are one of the most common and dangerous cybersecurity threats. Here's a comprehensive guide on how to protect yourself and your organization:

1. Email Verification
Always verify the sender's email address carefully. Phishers often use addresses that look similar to legitimate ones (e.g., support@paypa1.com instead of support@paypal.com).

2. Look for HTTPS
Before entering any sensitive information, ensure the website uses HTTPS. However, note that HTTPS alone doesn't guarantee a site is legitimate.

3. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Enable MFA on all your accounts. Even if your password is compromised, MFA adds an extra layer of security.

4. Security Awareness Training
Regularly train employees to recognize phishing attempts. Simulated phishing exercises can be particularly effective.

5. Email Filtering
Implement robust email filtering solutions that can detect and quarantine suspicious emails before they reach users.

6. Report Suspicious Emails
Always report suspicious emails to your IT security team or use built-in reporting features in email clients.

Stay vigilant and remember: when in doubt, don't click!
